title: Split diagnose_pacman_hook_stall.sh, this session's NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md §1 target
objective: Take diagnose_pacman_hook_stall.sh from 493 lines to under the repo's 250-line cap, confirmed live via the mandatory dead-code check-in before any code was touched. Split into 6 sourced libs by function group, keeping run_one/cleanup/log_size/main together in the entry script because they share PACMAN_PID/LAST_ELAPSED across the EXIT trap -- a prior session (commit 2527fb3) already demonstrated splitting run_one out produces a real SC2153/SC2034 pair, not a suppressible false positive. Reach 100% line coverage on every one of the 7 resulting files via a PATH-shim test harness, refactoring specific lines only where kcov's xtrace-based instrumentation cannot see them (done-with-redirect / group-with-redirect / inline-awk), per the user's explicit choice to fix the code rather than the coverage tool.
acceptance_criteria: check_file_length.sh --all no longer lists diagnose_pacman_hook_stall.sh (12 files remain, down from 13); the entry script itself and all 6 libs are at or under 250 lines.

verify_shell_split.sh against the pre-split revision (79829ec) reports DIFFERENCE only for functions that were deliberately rewritten (capture_stall, descendant_pids, kill_tree, main, mem_available_mb, print_summary, validate_requirements) with each rewrite's reason documented in evidence; every other function moves verbatim.

Every one of the 6 new libs and the entry script reaches 100% line coverage via meta/scripts/shell_coverage.sh, with no suppression of any shellcheck or coverage finding -- genuine gaps get either a new test case or a documented, reviewed code change, never a # noqa/disable equivalent.

descendant_pids' array-mutation semantics (pids+=("$child") surviving across loop iterations in the current shell) are preserved exactly -- verified by an existing multi-level-tree test passing unchanged before and after any refactor of that function.

shellcheck passes with zero findings across all 17 changed files run together (matching the pre-commit hook's actual batched invocation), relying on .shellcheckrc's external-sources=true + source-path=SCRIPTDIR to resolve cross-file globals correctly rather than any -x flag or suppression.

Every test file, including the ones this session writes, also stays under the 250-line cap -- the entry-script subprocess test grew past it while adding coverage and had to be split into a shared fixture (pacman_hook_stall_entry_harness.sh) plus two test files, re-verified for identical coverage/assertion count and no new jscpd duplication after the split.
jscpd stays under the repo's 2% duplication threshold, measured in a clean git worktree with the new files copied in (not the live working tree, which reads high off vendored .venv).

No test allocates unbounded real memory or otherwise touches the live machine's actual pacman state -- PACMAN_BIN/PACMAN_LOG/CACHE_DIR/PACMAN_LOCK/LOAD_FLOOR_MB/LOAD_MIN_FREE_MB are all env-overridable and every test points them at a throwaway tmpdir and a small, bounded allocation.
New sourced libs carry a shebang and the git-index executable bit (git add --chmod=+x), matching the existing lib/hosts_guard_migrate.sh convention in the same directory.
out_of_scope: §3 (install_leechblock.sh / block_compulsive_opening.sh) -- explicitly deferred in NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md due to the deployed-/usr/local/-copy trap that would break every pacman invocation on this machine if split naively.

Any other file listed in NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md §4 as out of scope until the user says otherwise (setup_midnight_shutdown.sh, check_and_enable_services.sh, pacman_wrapper.sh, the Kotlin/Dart files, etc).
Running the script against a real pacman transaction on this machine -- only the PATH-shim harness and a fake-but-real pacman.orig subprocess were exercised.
Hardening require_root's sudo -E environment-preservation against a hypothetical future NOPASSWD sudoers rule -- noted as a risk in evidence, not acted on, since no such rule exists today.
verifier: bash meta/scripts/check_file_length.sh --all; bash meta/scripts/verify_shell_split.sh 79829ec <entry> <entry> <6 libs>; bash meta/scripts/shell_coverage.sh <test> <subject> for each of the 7 subjects; shellcheck on all 17 changed files together; jscpd in a clean detached worktree; pre-commit run --files on the full staged set.
